{{external media | width = 210px | float = right | headerimage=  | audio1 = [https://archive.org/download/160118_ACI16_Fraley/160118_ACI16_Fraley.mp3 Dr. Robb Fraley - Sharing The Stories Of Genetic Science And Its Relation To Food And Consumers], presentation audio by Dr. Fraley at the 2016 Agribusiness Council of Indiana Conference & Expo, January 18–19, 2016, Indianapolis, IN, USA | video1 = [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J4nfC-6hkDI Robert Fraley of Monsanto on National Geographic's Plan to Feed a World of 9 Billion], Climate One, Jun 19, 2014 }}

'''Robert Thomas Fraley''' (January 25, 1953, [[Danville, Illinois]]<ref name=gmo/>) was executive vice president and [[chief technology officer]] at [[Monsanto]], where he helped to develop the first genetically modified seeds. He retired from Monsanto in June 2018.  He advocates for the use of [[GMO]] products to address global [[food security|food insecurity]] and reduce the environmental footprint of agriculture.<ref name="Mulvany">{{cite news |last1=Mulvany |first1=Lydia |title=Robert Fraley retires, but will remain GMO evangelist |url=https://www.farmfutures.com/business/robert-fraley-retires-will-remain-gmo-evangelist |accessdate=30 November 2018 |work=Farm Futures |date=August 7, 2018}}</ref>

Fraley was also a technical adviser to the USDA.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Robin |first=Marie-Monique |title=The World According to Monsanto: Pollution, Corruption, and the Control of Our Food Supply |publisher=The New Press |year=2014 |isbn=978-1-59558-536-3 |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Fraley grew up on a farm near [[Hoopeston, Illinois]].<ref name=gmo>{{cite book|title=GMO Food: A Reference Handbook|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4TC4BAAAQBAJ&pg=PA188|accessdate=2018-02-02|year=2014|isbn=9781610696869|author=David E. Newton| publisher=Abc-Clio }}</ref> Fraley attended the [[University of Illinois]] for both his bachelors and PhD, the latter focused on microbiology and biochemistry, working with Professor Samuel Kaplan in the Department of Microbiology, and completed in 1979.<ref>{{Cite thesis|url=https://www.ideals.illinois.edu/handle/2142/68087|title = Intracytoplasmic Membrane Synthesis During the Cell Division Cycle of Rhodopseudomonas Sphaeroides|year = 1979|publisher = University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|last1 = Thomas|first1 = Fraley}}</ref> He did post-doctoral research in biophysics at the [[University of California-San Francisco]].<ref name="HuffPost">{{cite web | title=Dr. Robert T. Fraley | website=HuffPost | url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/author/dr-robert-fraley | access-date=2018-02-03}}</ref> By 1983 he was working at Monsanto, where he was able to use ''[[Agrobacterium tumefaciens]]'' to transfer genes conferring a selectable marker into the cells of petunia plants.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Fraley | first1 = Robert T. | display-authors = et al. | year = 1983 | title = Expression of bacterial genes in plant cells | url = http://www.pnas.org/content/80/15/4803.full.pdf | journal = Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. | volume = 80 | issue = 15| pages = 4803–07 | bibcode = 1983PNAS...80.4803F | pmid=6308651|pmc=384133|doi=10.1073/pnas.80.15.4803| doi-access = free }}</ref> Together with Stephen Rogers and Robert Horsch, he was able to produce petunia plants that were resistant to kanamycin.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Lohar |first=Prakash S. |title=Textbook of Biotechnology |publisher=MJP Publisher |year=2019 |pages=169 |language=en}}</ref>

== Recognition ==

* In 1988 Fraley was elected a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name="Duncan">{{cite news |last1=Duncan |first1=David Ewing |title=Where the brainiacs are, and pharma isn't |url=https://money.cnn.com/2010/03/01/news/companies/pharma_aaas.fortune/index.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100303163428/http://money.cnn.com/2010/03/01/news/companies/pharma_aaas.fortune/index.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 3, 2010 |accessdate=30 November 2018 |work=CNN Money |date=March 3, 2010}}</ref>
* Fraley received [[The Progressive Farmer]]'s Man of the Year in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schattenberg |first=Paul |date=2013-06-19 |title=2013 World Food Prize laureates announced |url=https://agrilifetoday.tamu.edu/2013/06/19/2013-world-food-prize/ |access-date=2023-06-13 |website=AgriLife Today |language=en-US}}</ref>
* In 1999 he was awarded he [[National Medal of Technology]] by President [[Bill Clinton]].<ref name="White House">{{cite news |title=PRESIDENT CLINTON ANNOUNCES RECIPIENTS OF NATION'S HIGHEST SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY HONORS |url=https://clintonwhitehouse3.archives.gov/WH/EOP/OSTP/html/19981211.html |accessdate=30 November 2018 |work=The White House |date=December 8, 1998}}</ref>
* In 2008, he received the [[NAS Award for the Industrial Application of Science]] "for developing technologies that enabled the production of the world's first transgenic crops."<ref name="NAS">{{cite web |title=NAS Award for the Industrial Application of Science |url=http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/industrial-application-of-science.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111126050125/http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/industrial-application-of-science.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 26, 2011 |accessdate=30 November 2018 |website=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref>
* In 2009, he received the [[Biotechnology Heritage Award]] from the [[Biotechnology Industry Organization]] (BIO) and the [[Chemical Heritage Foundation]].<ref name="Biotechnology">{{cite web|title=Biotechnology Heritage Award|url=https://www.sciencehistory.org/biotechnology-heritage-award|website=Science History Institute|date=31 May 2016|accessdate=22 March 2018}}</ref>
* Fraley won the 2013 [[World Food Prize]] for "breakthrough achievements in founding, developing, and applying modern agricultural biotechnology".<ref name="WFP">{{cite web |title=2013 - Van Montagu, Chilton, Fraley |url=https://www.worldfoodprize.org/en/laureates/2010__2017_laureates/2013__van_montagu_chilton_fraley/ |website=The World Food Prize |date=2013 |accessdate=30 November 2018 |archive-date=25 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190725082847/https://www.worldfoodprize.org/en/laureates/2010__2017_laureates/2013__van_montagu_chilton_fraley/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Pollack">{{cite news |last1=Pollack |first1=Andrew |title=Executive at Monsanto Wins Global Food Honor |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/06/20/business/monsanto-executive-is-among-world-food-prize-winners.html |accessdate=30 November 2018 |work=The New York Times |date=June 19, 2013}}</ref>
*Fraley was inducted as a Laureate of [https://thelincolnacademyofillinois.org/ The Lincoln Academy of Illinois] and awarded the [[The Lincoln Academy of Illinois|Order of Lincoln]] (the State’s highest honor) by the Governor of Illinois on June 19, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|last=The Lincoln Academy of Illinois|date=9 January 2020|title=56th Laureate Convocation - Chicago History Museum|work=The Lincoln Academy of Illinois|url=https://thelincolnacademyofillinois.org/2020-laureates-announced-by-gov-pritzker/|access-date=|language=en-US|archive-date=14 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200514160602/https://thelincolnacademyofillinois.org/2020-laureates-announced-by-gov-pritzker/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
